summary.name: Gradescope
summary.one_liner: Gradescope is a web-based platform for administering and grading paper-based, digital, and code assessments, with rubrics, analytics, and grade export.
use_cases: grading programming assignments with an autograder
collecting student PDF or photo submissions
summary.what_it_does: Gradescope lets instructors administer and grade assessments whether online or in class, supporting both variable-length assignments like problem sets and projects and fixed-template assignments like quizzes and exams. Instructors can scan paper work or accept student uploads of PDFs, photos, or code from GitHub and Bitbucket. Grading uses flexible rubrics, one-click feedback, and an autograder for code, with inline comments for manual review. Bubble sheets are auto-graded against an answer key, and per-question and per-rubric analytics are available. Grades can be sent to students or exported to a gradebook.
notable: Answer groups and AI-assisted grading, available under the Institutional license
Autograder support for code submissions from GitHub and Bitbucket
Bubble sheet scanning that separates batches by test version
Per-question and per-rubric analytics and item analysis
caveats: AI-assisted grading and answer groups require the Institutional license
Page says grading is 'for free' in the meta description but does not detail free tier limits
